fieldMarks: Small, slim, gray-brown lizard with keeled scales, short legs, a long tail and a fold of small scales along each side; up to about 3.9 in snout-vent (WDFW).
Brown back with black spots forming transverse bands; white spots on the edges of side scales (WDFW).
Brown eyes; underside light with dark pigment on the lateral edges of each scale (WDFW).
Males have a broader, more triangular head; hatchlings are plain brown or have one line of dark spots down the midline (WDFW).
behavior: Active by day but secretive; usually found by turning rocks or woody debris (WDFW).
Tail is easily shed when threatened (WDFW).
Eats insects, ticks, spiders, millipedes and snails; litters average 4-6 (NatureServe).
Hibernates in winter; in British Columbia individuals did not make long moves between summer habitat and hibernation sites (NatureServe).
habitat: Grassy, brushy or rocky openings in forest, clearcuts and stream margins; rock walls, rock piles and woody debris in lightly developed areas (WDFW; NatureServe).
range: Southern British Columbia including Vancouver Island, south through western Washington and Oregon to west-central coastal California and the central Sierra Nevada, and in the Rockies to northern Idaho and western Montana, with disjunct populations in south-central Oregon, northeastern California and northwestern Nevada (NatureServe).

lookalikes.name: Southern alligator lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger (up to 5.5 in snout-vent), yellow or gold eyes, and no dark pigment on the lateral edges of the belly scales (WDFW).
